log.text: Gholdengo used Make It Rain → Sneasler

decisions.rationale: Lead Whimsicott and Gholdengo to establish Tailwind while threatening Mega Gardevoir, Sneasler, and Sinistcha with spread pressure. Arcanine provides Intimidate and disruption against the physical mode; Milotic is the stabilizing back-line answer to Incineroar and boosted physical attackers. Avoid exposing Tyranitar into the revealed special-pressure combination.
decisions.notebook: Opponent’s preferred mode is Mega Gardevoir special spread pressure paired with Sneasler Close Combat, with Incineroar disruption and Skarmory Tailwind as alternate support. Sinistcha may redirect and sustain. Preserve Milotic for physical stabilization and avoid relying on it into repeated double-targeting without Tailwind. Whimsicott should prioritize safely establishing Tailwind. Gholdengo is the primary immediate pressure piece; Arcanine supplies Intimidate and Incineroar disruption. Avoid Mega Tyranitar into the Gardevoir/Sneasler combination.

decisions.rationale: Lead Sneasler+Gardevoir: Sneasler OHKOs Tyranitar with Close Combat and double-into Gholdengo with Gardevoir's Shadow Ball; Gardevoir Megas for Pixilate spread. Incineroar (Intimidate/Fake Out/Parting Shot) and Dedenne (Choice Scarf Thunderbolt for Milotic) in back. Avoids leading Intimidate into Milotic's Competitive.
decisions.notebook: Opponent: Milotic Bold Competitive Sitrus (never lower its stats; Scald/Ice Beam/Haze/Protect). Whimsicott Prankster sash Tailwind/Encore/Moonblast/Helping Hand. Tyranitar-Mega Adamant Rock Slide/Crunch/Low Kick/Protect, Sand Stream. Gholdengo Life Orb Good-as-Gold Nasty Plot/Shadow Ball/Make It Rain/Protect. Arcanine Careful Shuca Intimidate Flare Blitz/Snarl/Will-O-Wisp/Protect. Lopunny Jolly Black Belt Limber Fake Out/HJK/Triple Axel/Protect. My plan: Sneasler Close Combat OHKOs Tyranitar; Sneasler Shadow Claw + Gardevoir Shadow Ball double KOs Gholdengo; Dedenne Thunderbolt chunks Milotic (not OHKO); Sneasler Close Combat is NEUTRAL on Arcanine (Fighting vs Fire), so use Gardevoir/Incineroar vs Arcanine. Respect Whimsicott Encore on Protect. Keep Incineroar off Milotic leads to avoid Competitive boost.

decisions.rationale: Whimsicott safely establishes Tailwind with priority, covering Sneasler’s uncertain Speed and enabling Gholdengo afterward. Make It Rain applies immediate spread pressure to both foes, especially Gardevoir, while Gholdengo is immune to Sneasler’s Close Combat and Gardevoir’s Hyper Voice.

I double Gholdengo with Sneasler Shadow Claw + Mega Gardevoir Shadow Ball to remove it; combined ~71-157% likely KOs a Life Orb Modest set. If Gholdengo Protects/Nasty Plots, Gardevoir stays safe and we still remove it. Mega evolving boosts the Shadow Ball KO odds.

Dedenne's moves are all resisted/immune vs Steel/Ghost Gholdengo and weak vs Whimsicott, so Incineroar offers more immediate pressure despite being slow.

Arcanine is Fire-type so it can't be burned; Dedenne may fall to its Flare Blitz regardless, so make its turn count.

reflections.summary: Won game 3 and the series 2-1. The decisive factor was the Milotic-Arcanine endgame: Milotic’s Scald heavily punished Incineroar, while Arcanine survived long enough to finish it. Whimsicott’s Moonblast also removed Dedenne and Sneasler. The opening was inefficient: Gholdengo was exposed to Incineroar’s super-effective Flare Blitz, Encore failed, and Will-O-Wisp was used into a Fire-type. The chosen four and sets were therefore serviceable but not cleanly optimized. Milotic, Arcanine’s defensive profile, Whimsicott’s Focus Sash, and Moonblast were good preparation; Gholdengo’s matchup and the Fire-immune Will-O-Wisp plan were poor. No Mega was brought or evolved, so Mega Tyranitar’s suitability cannot be confirmed from this game. The evidence does not establish a specific between-game adjustment, though the final-game defensive plan succeeded; the series win is authoritative and there were no recorded decision errors.
reflections.adjustment: Against a rematch, prioritize Milotic and Arcanine earlier as the Incineroar answer, preserve Milotic as the stabilizer, and avoid spending Arcanine’s turn on Will-O-Wisp against Fire-types. Reconsider Gholdengo as an opener or bring stronger protection for it from Flare Blitz and Fake Out. Retain Whimsicott if its Moonblast pressure is valuable, but do not rely on Encore as the primary plan and protect the opportunity to establish Tailwind. Re-evaluate the four brought rather than automatically omitting Mega Tyranitar; however, the available evidence is insufficient to claim Tyranitar, Basculegion, Tauros, Furfrou, or Chimecho was definitively better. Sets for the omitted draft options were not supplied, so their preparation cannot be fairly judged.
reflections.notebook: Incineroar is Intimidate with Fake Out, Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, and Flare Blitz; it carries Sitrus Berry. Fire-types are immune to Will-O-Wisp, so use direct damage, Snarl, Protect, or Milotic pressure instead. Incineroar’s pivoting and Intimidate make Milotic a valuable countermeasure; preserve Milotic when possible. Sneasler revealed Focus Sash, Unburden, Protect, Close Combat, Dire Claw, and Shadow Claw; remove it before it can exploit its speed boost. Dedenne revealed Choice Scarf with Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Dazzling Gleam, and Super Fang, making it an immediate speed-control and disruption threat. Mega Gardevoir was used with Hyper Voice, Moonblast, Shadow Ball, and Protect; prepare for strong spread and Fairy damage. Whimsicott’s Moonblast is useful against this offensive core, but Tailwind should be established only when its survival is protected. Gholdengo is vulnerable to Incineroar’s Fire pressure and should not be exposed without a clear payoff. The defensive Milotic-Arcanine pairing was effective; future preparation should preserve that structure while replacing the ineffective Will-O-Wisp expectation and improving the opening matchup.
